 Proposed Rule Would End SNAPs Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility in Arkansas, Other States
 November 18, 2026    |  
 Elizabeth (Izzy) Montgomery 
 On November 10, the U.S. Department of Agricultures (USDA) Food and Nutrition Administration published a proposed rule that would effectively eliminate broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE) for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
 BBCE is a state policy option that allows households to become categorically eligible for food benefits under SNAP if they also qualify for a non-cash benefit or service funded by the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program. Arkansas is among 46 states and territories that use BBCE, although its approach is limited. Unlike most states, Arkansas retains SNAPs federal gross income limit of 130% of the federal poverty level (FPL). It also retains SNAPs asset limit, which caps a households countable resources such as cash and bank accounts at $3,000, or $4,750 for households with an elderly or disabled family member, and allows only a temporary increase in that limit for certain households. Most states use BBCE to raise SNAPs income limit above the federal income limit and eliminate the SNAP asset limit.
 Under the proposed federal rule, categorical eligibility through TANF would be limited to households that receive TANF assistance, which generally consists of cash benefits but can include certain non-cash supportive services such as job training and informational brochures. Under current rules, receipt of a TANF-funded brochure, for example, is treated as a TANF benefit that can establish SNAP eligibility through BBCE. Under the proposed rule, however, most non-cash services would no longer qualify a household for SNAP. The USDA estimates that 6.3 million people (nearly 18% of SNAP recipients) would no longer receive SNAP benefits in fiscal year 2029, the first year the rule would fully be in effect, because their household income or resources would exceed the federal eligibility limit.
 How Arkansas Uses BBCE
 Arkansas retains SNAPs federal 130% FPL gross income limit to determine BBCE for most households. For households with an elderly or disabled member, Arkansas applies a 165% FPL threshold for BBCE eligibility. These households are generally exempt from the gross income test under regular federal SNAP rules, meaning those above 165% FPL may still qualify if they meet the net income and asset limits. SNAPs net income limit requires that income after allowable deductions, such as for housing and childcare costs, be at or below 100% of the FPL. State law also limits Arkansass ability to exceed SNAPs federal gross income standards. Arkansas is one of only a handful of states that have kept an asset limit in place. Like many other states, Arkansas confers BBCE by providing SNAP applicants with a TANF-funded brochure.
 Under Act 675 of 2023 and rules subsequently implemented by the Arkansas Department of Human Services, Arkansas allows a temporary increase in the SNAP asset limit to $5,500 for certain households for 12 consecutive months, no more than once every five years. The temporary increase allows households to build modest savings without immediately losing SNAP eligibility.
 How the Proposed Rule Would Impact Arkansas
 Because Arkansass BBCE is established through a non-cash TANF benefit, the proposed rule would eliminate the federal mechanism supporting the temporary increase in SNAP asset limits authorized under Act 675. Also, households that currently qualify for BBCE would need to meet SNAPs net income limit in addition to the gross income limit that already applies to most households.
 Notably, children in households that lose SNAP eligibility could also lose automatic certification for free school meals, a mechanism known as direct certification. These students would no longer be directly certified through SNAP but could still qualify for direct certification through Medicaid eligibility or remain eligible for free or reduced-price meals based on household income.
 The proposed rule could also affect schools participating in the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP), which allows eligible schools to offer free meals to all students without collecting individual applications. Students directly certified for free meals through SNAP or Medicaid count toward a schools identified student percentage, which determines CEP eligibility and reimbursement rates.
 Removing BBCE could also increase administrative responsibilities for states. States using BBCE would have to apply SNAPs income and resource tests to more households to determine eligibility. Because Arkansas already applies an asset test, the impact on the eligibility determination process may not be as significant in Arkansas as in states that eliminated asset tests under BBCE, though it could require updates to eligibility systems and additional staff training.
 The announcement of the proposed rule comes as Arkansass share of SNAP administrative costs has risen from 50% to 75% under H.R. 1, the 2025 budget reconciliation law, and as the state works to lower its payment error rate (the share of SNAP benefit dollars issued in the wrong amount) before benefit cost sharing begins in October 2027. Under H.R. 1, states with error rates of 6% or higher will be required to pay a share of SNAP benefit costs, which have historically been federally funded. The USDA reported in June that Arkansass error rate was nearly 9% .
 Public comments on the rule may be submitted through December 10.
 For more on this topic, see our SNAP explainer .
 Elizabeth (Izzy) Montgomery, MPA, is a senior health policy analyst at ACHI.
